newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's CVG, Placer Dome sign Cristinas deal.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CVG, Placer Dome sign Cristinas deal.

text.p: CARACAS, Feb 6 - Venezuela's state-owned industrial holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) and Canadian mining company Placer Dome Inc signed Thursday a contract worth $576 million for the Las Cristinas gold mine project.

Placer Dome President for Latin America William Hayes said "we're very happy, we've reached final agreement on the three main contracts, all that is remaining are environmental permits and a tax exemption ... which we expect in a few months."
The contracts that remained to be signed included one on shareholding and another on electricity supply.
The tax exemption is worth $50 million and Hayes told reporters: "We'll have to revisit the theme if we don't get the exemption."
CVG President Elias Ynaty said "we're looking for the most rapid way to get it".
Once the environmental permits are given, construction will take 24 months, with production due to start in early 1999.
Production of gold is seen at 650,000 ounces for the first year, levelling out to 450,000 ounces of gold per year on average for at least 16 years, Hayes said.
Placer holds a 70 percent interest in the Las Cristinas project in south-eastern Bolivar state and CVG the remaining 30 percent. Construction was initially set to have begun in December.
Hayes also said "conversations we're having with banks about 250 million dollars of financing are very well advanced."
He said the Caracas-based Andean Development Corporation (CAF) was very interested "although we're speaking with other banks."

Up to 50 percent of the gold produced will be exported and refined abroad in copper concentrate, Hayes said. Of the other 50 percent, 15 percent will remain with the Central Bank and 85 percent can be exported or freely sold.
